speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long your child has been experiencing nosebleeds, petechiae, and bleeding from the mouth or gums? Also, has there been any recent illness, fever, or bruising without a clear cause?

text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor

text: Has the child experienced any recent viral infections or fevers, and are there any symptoms like fatigue or bone pain? I also need to know if there is any swelling of the lymph nodes or liver.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the child have any history of easy bruising or bleeding after minor injuries, and have you noticed any enlarged spleen or liver? Also, has the child been taking any new medications or supplements recently?

speaker: Patient

The absence of fever and bone pain makes leukemia less likely, but the petechiae and mucous bleeding strongly suggest a platelet issue like ITP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells. Coagulation Profile: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal). Special Test (ELISA Binding Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal platelet count and coagulation profile, combined with the deficient GIIb/IIIa receptors, confirm a functional platelet defect.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia
